question.worked_solution:
First, we find the hyperbolic identity that corresponds to the following double-angle formula for cosine: 

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡2\theta =1-2{sin}^{2}⁡\theta 
$$

Using Osborn's rule, we get the following double-angle formula for the hyperbolic cosine:

$$
\operatorname{cosh}⁡2\theta =1+2{sinh}^{2}⁡\theta 
$$

We can rearrange the above formula as

$$
{sinh}^{2}⁡\theta =\frac{1}{2}(\operatorname{cosh}⁡2\theta -1).
$$

Letting $\theta =\frac{x}{2}$, we have

$$
{sinh}^{2}⁡(\frac{x}{2})=\frac{1}{2}(\operatorname{cosh}⁡x-1).
$$

We can now integrate as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\pi }8{sinh}^{2}⁡(\frac{x}{2})\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }8\cdot \frac{1}{2}(\operatorname{cosh}⁡x-1)\,\text{d}x \\  & =4{\int }_{0}^{\pi }(\operatorname{cosh}⁡x-1)\,\text{d}x \\  & =4(\operatorname{sinh}⁡x-x)\,{|}_{0}^{\pi } \\  & =4[(\operatorname{sinh}⁡\pi -\pi )-(\operatorname{sinh}⁡0-0)] \\  & =4\operatorname{sinh}⁡(\pi )-4\pi \end{aligned}
$$
